question: What was the term for land revenue in the Chola kingdom?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kadamai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kadamai** was the term used for **land revenue** in the **Chola kingdom**. It referred to the tax or dues collected from the landowners.
 
• The **Chola dynasty**, which ruled southern India from approximately the 9th century to the 13th century CE, had a well-organized revenue system for the administration of its vast territories.
 
• Land revenue under the Cholas was typically collected from agricultural land and was a major source of income for the kingdom. The term **Kadamai** denoted the obligation of farmers or landowners to pay taxes to the state or local authorities.
 
• Revenue officers called **Vettiyan** were appointed to collect Kadamai. These officials ensured compliance with tax obligations and maintained records of the land and its productivity.
 
• The revenue system under the Cholas also included taxes on irrigation facilities, which were extensively developed during their reign to support agriculture.
 
• **Kadamai** was an essential part of the Chola administrative structure, reflecting their efficient governance and resource management practices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chola Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Chola dynasty was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in Indian history, with its rule extending from the 9th century to the 13th century CE.
 
• The Cholas were known for their remarkable contributions to **art, architecture, literature, and administration**.
 
• Their capital was located at **Thanjavur**, and they expanded their kingdom to include parts of South India, Sri Lanka, and Southeast Asia.
 
 
 
• **Land Revenue System:**
 
 
• Under the Chola administration, land was classified based on its fertility and productivity, and taxes were levied accordingly.
 
• The tax rate varied but typically ranged from one-sixth to one-fourth of the produce.
 
• Irrigation facilities, including tanks and canals, played a crucial role in enhancing agricultural productivity and were often taxed separately.
 
 
 
• **Other Revenue Terms:**
 
 
• **Vetti:** A form of forced labor or tribute, often paid in goods or services instead of money.
 
• **Cess Tax:** While not specific to the Chola kingdom, the term is generally used for taxes levied for specific purposes, such as education or health.
 
• **Ladder Tax:** This term is unrelated to the Chola kingdom and typically refers to taxes levied in other historical contexts, such as those imposed on the use of ladders in medieval Europe.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Kadamai:**
 
 
• The term **Kadamai** highlights the structured approach the Cholas took to governance, ensuring a steady revenue stream to support their administrative and military needs.
 
• It also reflects the interdependence between the state and the agricultural sector, which was the backbone of the economy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Chola dynasty's efficient administrative system included local governance through village assemblies called **sabhas**. These assemblies played a role in managing revenue collection and agricultural activities.
 
• The Cholas constructed numerous irrigation facilities, such as the **Kallanai Dam**, which ensured a reliable water supply for agriculture and contributed to their economic prosperity.
 
• The Chola rulers were patrons of art and architecture, and the revenue collected through Kadamai funded the construction of grand temples like the **Brihadeeswara Temple**.
 
• The Chola dynasty's governance model, including its revenue system, influenced subsequent South Indian kingdoms and contributed to the region's historical legacy.
